claims.text: The proposed intervention is a machine-learning prediction framework incorporating high-throughput DFT calculations and empirical design parameters.
This intervention can overcome limitations in determining melting temperatures of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
This intervention can overcome limitations in determining enthalpies and entropies of fusion of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
This intervention can overcome limitations in determining volume changes upon melting and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework applies to high-temperature solid and liquid states over a large HEA compositional space.
Configurational entropy, mixing enthalpy, and Gibbs free energy are the mediating thermodynamic quantities in the proposed prediction mechanism.
Configurational entropy, mixing enthalpy, and Gibbs free energy affect the formation of single-phase solid solutions in high-entropy alloys.
Learning the effects of these thermodynamic quantities on single-phase formation enables accurate prediction of melting, fusion, volume-change, and liquid-state properties.
The proposed framework will improve predictive accuracy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The proposed framework will improve the efficiency of thermodynamic-property determination relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Approximately 10^8 possible HEAs can be developed from about 64 elements.
Model accuracy may be limited by training-data quality and quantity and by the complexity of the underlying thermodynamic processes.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing predicted melting temperature, fusion properties, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties with experimental measurements.
A significant deviation between predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
